newsitem.title: UK: Cash paper Brent eases, physical maintains gains.
newsitem.headline: Cash paper Brent eases, physical maintains gains.

text.p: Cash paper Brent eased further on Monday afternoon as spread sellers in particular got the upper hand.
Feb/Mar and Mar/Apr Brent both narrowed to trade at +52 cents as the outright market fell 20 cents on the day to $23.25 a barrel.
But North Sea physical premiums held higher values after active trade late last week cleared out a raft of cargoes loading in the first half of January.
Friday saw some 12 million barrels of North Sea crudes moved, mostly to refiners.
Prompt CFDS, for the balance of this week, slipped 5-10 cents versus February to Feb +30 cents reflecting a weaker Jan/Feb spread of about +45 cents.
North Sea sweet cargoes for January saw offers coming in slightly higher than the improved levels last traded.
Two Ekofisk cargoes for mid-January asked Dated Brent +25 cents. Statfjord was still valued around Brent +40 cents.
Traders said an open arbitrage into the U.S. would continue to provide support to the physical North Sea market.
The arb narrowed a little on Monday, coming in 10 cents to $1.55 by 1730 GMT.
Dated Brent traded at Jan -13 cents on Friday and was restricted to a quotes related sale on Monday.
One Brent date, a Jan 7-9, was kept voluntarily on Monday.
